The main takeaway from our work is that
the LON-ClP axis is essential for the maintenance of mitochondrial bioenergetics and ROS homeostasis, and that its dysfunction could be the primary cause of mitochondrial ROS toxicity in PD.
the LON-ClP proteolytic axis is an important quality control mechanism that protects against ROS accumulation in PD and other neurodegenerative diseases.
